items.author: NMTri1110
items.descZh: WillderCore 是一款基于 MIT 协议开源的上下文同步中间层，旨在解决分布式应用、AI 代理与团队之间的状态同步难题。其核心功能是构建一个统一的上下文层，实现跨应用、跨智能体的实时数据协调，并在每一次调用中实施严格的访问控制。项目亮点在于其将安全管控粒度细化至单次调用，并结合 memoryservice、mcp 及 prisma 等模块实现了高效的实时同步架构，同时提供 CLI 工具与自托管支持以降低部署门槛。该方案特别适用于需要构建多智能体协同工作流、跨系统实时状态同步，以及对安全性和实时性有严苛要求的团队级 AI 开发场景。
items.quote: 同步您的应用程序、代理和团队的上下文层。每次通话访问控制，实时协调。
items.titleZh: Show HN: Willder，一个同步应用、智能体和团队的开源上下文层。

items.descZh: 本文介绍的是一款功能极其强大的免费在线文本大小写转换与多功能处理工具，其核心定位是提供完全本地化、无需上传文件且免注册的浏览器端文本转换服务。该工具不仅覆盖了句子大小写、遵循AP/APA等规范的标题大小写、全大写/全小写，还深度支持 camelCase、PascalCase、snake_case 等多种编程命名风格及 URL slug 生成。其突出亮点在于所有处理均在浏览器本地完成，确保了敏感数据（如源代码、客户资料）的绝对安全，并提供 locale-aware 精确转换（如支持土耳其语带点I的无损转换），同时内置了丰富的文本格式化、排序、正则替换以及 JSON/YAML/CSV 数据互转等开发者实用工具。该工具通过键盘快捷键（如 Ctrl/Cmd+Enter 快速复制）大幅提升了操作效率，是程序员、文案编辑、办公人员进行文本清洗、格式转换及趣味字符生成的终极工具。

items.title: Show HN: Calculators for token costs and Claude Code API budgets
items.desc: description: Estimate a month of Claude Code API spend on ModelFold from published Claude token rates. Presets are planning assumptions, not a subscription price. title: Claude Code monthly cost estimator ModelFold image: https://modelfold.ai/docs/og.png Loading template… Claude Code monthly cost estimator This estimates API token spend when Claude Code calls ModelFold. It is not the price of a Claude subscription. Presets are planning assumptions you can edit. Each request is rounded up, then multiplied by days and requests. [Pricing page](/pricing) Usage preset LightShort edits on most weekdaysRegularA working day of codingHeavyLong agent sessions Claude model Claude Sonnet 4.6 Days per month Requests per day Average input tokens Average output tokens Estimated month $61.60 12,320 credits 1,760 requests in the month Per day: 560 credits · $2.80 Per request: 7 credits [Claude Code setup guide](https://modelfold.ai/docs/en/aiagent/claudecode) A preset is not a measurement of your account. Change the token counts to match the context you actually send. Cache reads and reasoning tokens follow the API rules. __Same usage on other Claude models__ Claude Haiku 5.5 1,760 credits $8.80 Claude Haiku 4.5 5,280 credits $26.40 Claude Sonnet 4.5 12,320 credits $61.60 Claude Sonnet 4.6 12,320 credits $61.60 Claude Sonnet 5 12,320 credits $61.60 Claude Sonnet 5.5 12,320 credits $61.60 Claude Opus 4.5 21,120 credits $105.60 Claude Opus 4.6 21,120 credits $105.60 Claude Opus 4.7 21,120 credits $105.60 Claude Opus 5.5 22,880 credits $114.40 Claude Opus 4.8 28,160 credits $140.80 Claude Opus 5 28,160 credits $140.80 Claude Fable 5 56,320 credits $281.60 Questions Is this the Claude Pro subscription? items.author: modelfold
items.descZh: 本文介绍的 ModelFold Claude Code 月度费用估算器，是一款专为预测在 ModelFold 平台上调用 Claude API 的代币消耗成本而设计的预算工具，其显示的费用仅为 API 使用费，而非 Anthropic 官方的 Claude 订阅价格。该工具的核心功能是支持用户通过自定义参数或选用内置的“轻量”、“常规”和“重度”三种预设场景，模拟每月天数、日均请求数以及输入输出代币量来计算总花费。亮点在于提供了具体的性能与价格对比数据，例如在常规预设下，使用 Claude Sonnet 4.6 模型每月 1,760 次请求的估算成本为 61.60 美元（折合 12,320 积分），而重度使用 Claude Fable 5 的成本则高达 281.60 美元，且明确标注失败生成不收费。该工具适用于计划通过 ModelFold 兼容端点部署 Claude Code 的开发团队，用于在实际接入前进行精细化的财务预测与成本控制。
items.quote: 根据公开的 Claude token 费率，估算 ModelFold 一个月的 Claude Code API 开销。预设仅为规划假设，并非订阅价格。

items.title: Show HN: ZTHR – what replaces code review when AI agents write all the code
items.desc: description: ZTHR: Zero Trust – High Reliability. A pattern language for software built by AI, where quality comes from the environment, not the author. title: ZTHR: A Pattern Language for Autonomous Software Delivery image: https://zthr.ai/og.png [Skip to content](main) Zero Trust – High Reliability AI writes the code. _The factory proves it._ ZTHR is a pattern language for software built by AI. Nothing is trusted because it says so, and quality comes from the environment the author works in, not from the author. [Start simple](eli5) [Explore the map](map) [Read the paper](paper) [See a working example](/reference) [Read the case](/reference/case) GENERATOR any model JIG governed parts GO NO GO gauges proven to fail rejected: try again, as often as it takes INTENT can users still do it? A SERVING = BUILT every escape becomes a new fixture ZTHR00 · GENERATE · JIG · GAUGE · INTENT · SERVE [Depth 11 minTL;DROne paragraph. What ZTHR is and why it works.](tldr) [Depth 24 minExplain it simplyThe bookshelf factory. No software knowledge needed.](eli5) [Depth 325 minEngineerThe two principles, the concept map and all thirtythree patterns.](principles) [Depth 490 minArchitectAuthority, the learning loops, failure tracing, economics and the full paper.](system) See it working: the Student Advocate [Map: how it fits together start hereEvery part of the example on one page: the app, its admin, the evidence, the docs and the case.](/reference) [The case writeupWhat an AI factory can build, and what it is worth: business and technical.](/reference/case) [About the app exampleA reference app built entirely by agents under ZTHR fixtures: what it does and who it is for.](/advocate) [Use the app liveSign in as any of twelve sample students, each a private copy for two hours.](/studentadvocate/) [App admin liveCatalog, moderation, scouts, admissions and outcome measures.](/studentadvocate/admin/) [Evidence factoryGates, walks, every test, mutation, the sensitivedata trace and the block library.](/reference/factory/) [The full source GitHubThe app, the blocks, the gates, the pipeline and every journey card.](https://github.com/russlittle/ZTHR/tree/referenceimplementation) [Discussion forumQuestions, experience reports and objections, in the open.](https://github.com/russlittle/ZTHR/discussions) Read it as a document [Executive summary 2 pagesThe problem, the two principles, how it works and how to judge it.](summary) [The brief 5 pagesBoth principles in depth, all six families, governance and limits.](brief) [The full paper 33 patternsEvery pattern with its forces and consequences, failure tracing and economics.](paper) TL;DR The whole idea in one paragraph Generating code is now nearly free. Deciding whether it is right is not. So stop asking people to read every diff, and build a factory that cannot be fooled: governed parts that limit what can be built, checks proven to fail on the defects they exist to catch, and statements of user intent the author cannot rewrite. Let the models try as many times as it takes. Ship only what passes. Turn every miss into a new check. Two principles _A_Symmetric Zero Trust No author, reviewer, model, operator or report gains authority by asserting success. A claim counts only on evidence the claimant does not control. _B_The Fixture Inversion Quality moves out of the author's skill and into the environment. Generators iterate until the fixtures are satisfied. The question every reviewer asks instead of "is this code good?" ⌖INTENTA Which fixture forces that, and has it been shown to bite? Thirtythree patterns in six families [Construction P1–6What can be built at all.](patterns)[Verification P7–14That code meets its properties, and the checks work.](patterns)[Intent P15–18That users can still do what they came to do.](patterns)[Independence P19–22That a reader without the author's story agrees.](patterns)[Operational P23–27That work keeps moving and what ships is what passed.](patterns)[Runtime and environment P28–33That models and integrations hold at the moment of use.](patterns) Cite this work Little, R. (2026). ZTHR: A Pattern Language for Autonomous Software Delivery (Version 1.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23826734 Copy citation TitleZTHR Sheet1 / 9 DatumUser intent AuthorRuss Little Depth 2 · Explain it simply The bookshelf factory Everything in ZTHR is in this story. The software version just has more parts. You have a robot that can build a thousand bookshelves a day. It is fast, it is getting smarter, and it always says it did a great job. Sometimes it is right. Sometimes the shelf wobbles. You could check every shelf by hand. You would never keep up, and by the fivehundredth shelf you would miss things. This is code review when AI writes the code: the reviewer becomes the bottleneck or a rubber stamp. So you build a jig: a frame that holds the wood so the shelf can only go together one way. In software: a shared foundation and a catalog of tested parts, so the robot does not reinvent the locks and hinges every time. Then you build a gauge: a tester that tries every shelf and says fits or does not fit. And you test the tester. You hand it a broken shelf on purpose and make sure it says no. A tester that never says no is not a tester. You do not only check each board. You check what people want: can you put books on it? That is user intent. It is written down where the robot cannot change it. Now the robot can try as many times as it needs. Bad shelves go back. Only shelves that pass every test leave the factory. Trying again is cheap. Shipping a bad shelf is not. When a bad shelf ever slips through, you do not only fix that shelf. You build a new test so that kind of mistake can never slip through again. The factory gets stricter every week, and so does everything it builds. _A_ Nobody is believed just because they say it worked. items.title: Show HN: AI Frothiness Index. Daily reading of how stretched the AI boom is
items.desc: description: A daily 0–100 gauge of how stretched the AI boom is, built only from free public data: prices, borrowing, spending, speculation and real demand. Jag's AI Frothiness Index A daily 0–100 reading of how stretched the AI boom is, built only from free public data: stock prices, borrowing, hyperscaler spending, speculation, and real demand. 50 is normal for the last few decades; the dotcom peak is the yardstick for 100. – … 0 · Calm40 · Warm60 · Frothy80 · Bubble100 The index over time Weekly before 2018, daily since. Shaded bands mark Calm, Warm, Frothy and Bubble. Compare from a milestone: or any date The five pillars today Each pillar averages its indicators' percentiles. Real demand counts against froth: fastgrowing usage makes heavy spending more justified. Every indicator Percentile = where today's reading sits against that indicator's whole history up to today (100 = most stretched ever). Click a source to check the raw data. Bubble talk: the noise meter Not part of the index. How loudly people are talking and betting about an AI bubble over the last 28 days, compared with every 28day stretch since 2022\. Talk tends to peak before the top, not after. – Noise meter (0–100) Hacker News: "AI bubble" stories + comments per week Wikipedia: "AI bubble" article views per week Betting markets: odds the AI bubble bursts All AIthemed betting, last 24 hours Busiest AI markets today How it works Inputs: 19 indicators from free primary sources: FRED (St. Louis Fed), SEC EDGAR filings and fulltext search, Yahoo Finance prices, the npm registry, Y Combinator's company list, and the Ramp AI Index. No handentered numbers. Scoring: each reading becomes a percentile against that indicator's own history up to that day, so the past is scored without hindsight. Indicators flagged "inverted" (VIX, credit spreads) score higher when they are low, because calm markets mean complacency. Pillars and weights: Prices 30%, Borrowing & risk appetite 20%, Spending strain 20%, Speculation 15%. Real demand takes the remaining 15% as a counterweight: index = 0.85 × (weighted pillars) + 0.15 × (100 − demand). History: inputs join as their data begins, so the 1990s use only prices and borrowing; AIspecific inputs (SEC capex, npm, YC, Ramp) arrive after 2009–2023\. Slow data (quarterly filings) carries forward until the next release. Bands: under 40 Calm, 40–60 Warm, 60–80 Frothy, 80+ Bubble. Milestones: pick an event (or any date) under the chart to see how far the index and each pillar have moved since then. The data starts in 1997, so earlier AI milestones such as ELIZA (1966) or MYCIN (1970s) can't be compared. Share a comparison with a link like <since=20221130. Bubble talk is shown separately because it is contrarian: Hacker News mentions (Algolia API), Wikipedia views (Wikimedia API), and volume on Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold. Caveats A high reading says things are stretched, not when they will turn. Stretched markets can stay stretched for years. Official data is revised; history is rebuilt from today's vintage, not what was known at the time. Hyperscaler figures come from XBRL tags that differ between companies; a quarter counts when at least three of the five report. Kalshi has no AIbubble market, so only its overall AIthemed betting volume is counted. Manifold uses play money. This is a personal project. Nothing here is investment advice.
items.author: psiberaktiv
items.descZh: Jag's AI Frothiness Index 是一个每日更新的指标，用于量化AI热潮的过度程度，范围从0到100，完全基于免费公开数据，如股票价格、借贷、超大规模支出、投机和实际需求。该指数通过整合19个指标，包括来自FRED、SEC EDGAR和Yahoo Finance等来源的数据，采用加权计算得出分数，其中价格支柱占30%，借贷和风险偏好占20%，支出压力占20%，投机占15%，实际需求作为反向指标占15%以抵消泡沫。分数等级分为平静（低于40）、温暖（40-60）、泡沫状（60-80）和泡沫（80以上），帮助用户评估市场紧张程度。适用场景包括比较不同里程碑事件或日期的指数值，以分析AI市场趋势。亮点还包括独立的“Bubble talk”噪音计，衡量公众讨论AI泡沫的热度，数据源自Hacker News和维基百科等。
